about: True parameters of the subscriptions extension dataset in data/synthetic/, written by scripts/make_synthetic.py from src/mktstats/synth/. Do not edit by hand.
description: Monthly subscription program, three plans, sign-ups growing over two years, observed until observation_end. Weibull proportional-hazards churn in plan and onboarding; an intro offer that raises the hazard only before the landmark. Subscribers still active at observation_end are right-censored.
time_zero: The first billing date, when the 14-day trial ends: onboarding is completed (or not) during the trial, so it is known when the clock starts and no subscriber's group depends on how long they stayed (no immortal-time bias).

model.hazard: h(t | z) = h0(t) exp(eta), eta = -0.25 standard - 0.60 premium - 0.40 onboarded - u; H(t) = exp(eta) [exp(0.70 intro_offer) H0(min(t, 3)) + max(H0(t) - H0(3), 0)], H0(t) = (t / 14) ** 0.8, t in months of 30.4375 days
model.reference_group: basic plan, not onboarded, no intro offer
model.hidden_confounding_note: u = hidden_confounding * N(0, 1) adds to the log-odds of onboarding and subtracts from eta; the hazard ratios above are conditional on u.

covariates.independence: Onboarding depends on plan (and on u when hidden_confounding > 0) and nothing else; the intro offer is independent of plan, onboarding and u.

survival.by_intro_offer_note: the offer is independent of plan and onboarding

rmst.definition: RMST(t*) = integral of S(t) from 0 to t*: expected months subscribed within the first t* months
rmst.target_population: subscribers who did not complete onboarding
rmst.gain_target_definition: mean over the target population of RMST(24) with onboarding set to 1 minus with it set to 0; with hidden_confounding = 0 it equals the plan-weighted sum of the per-plan gains
rmst.discounting: each month subscribed at time t is worth (1 + monthly_discount) ** -t

decision.rule: call a subscriber who did not onboard when q * gain * margin > call_cost

tolerances.basis: How often each checkpoint rule of Module 14 holds when the reference solutions are run on data from other seeds of the same generator (n = 8,000, default settings). A rule that holds in nearly every seed passes on a correct solution and still fails on the wrong ones it targets. Intervals are named: 95% pointwise (exponential Greenwood) for Kaplan-Meier, 95% Wald confidence intervals for Cox hazard ratios, and the 95% bootstrap percentile interval (stratified by plan x onboarding, seed 14) for the RMST gain.

1000-1039.note: the seeds of the brief's prototype; this generator reproduces its draws

3000-3039.note: an independent check; checkpoints 3 and 5 failed together on the same seeds (3000, 3028, 3034, 3035, 3037), where the onboarding effect came out stronger than the truth by chance

tolerances.summary: Over 80 seeds: Kaplan-Meier truth 3 of 4 in 78, dashboards outside in 80; checkpoint 3 in 73 and its unadjusted check in 80; checkpoint 4 (3 of 4) in 80; checkpoint 5's truth inside in 72 (B = 100) and 73 (B = 200), the unadjusted gain outside in 80. Checkpoints 3 and 5 rest on one 95% interval each, so about 1 seed in 10 misses: roughly the nominal 5% plus some undercoverage of the percentile bootstrap. On the committed seed (2034) every rule holds with the reference in QUICK and FULL, and a correct solution reproduces the reference's numbers exactly.

rules.km_vs_truth: true S(t) at 6, 12, 18 and 24 months inside the 95% pointwise interval for at least 3 of 4; dashboards A and B outside it at 12 months
rules.checkpoint_3: true onboarding HR (0.670) inside its 95% CI and at least 2 of the 3 true HRs (standard, premium, onboarded) inside theirs; with onboarding alone, the truth outside the CI and the HR below the adjusted one
rules.checkpoint_4: at least 3 of 4 inside their 95% CIs: offer HR 2.014 before month 3, 1.0 after, onboarding HR 0.670 before and after
rules.checkpoint_5: true target-population gain (2.907 months) inside the 95% bootstrap percentile interval; the unadjusted Kaplan-Meier gain outside it
